### Position read
Opening position. We moved Red from (0,3) to (4,3), taking the lower-left center. No losses or eliminations.

### Our plan
Use Yellow to occupy (3,3) if the route remains open. This left-center column formation blocks Green’s direct horizontal access to the two right-center squares and creates a fast center-win threat. Expect Blue to contest one center; aim to secure the other three and build a capture or enclosure against the intruder.

### Opponent tendencies
No moves observed yet.

### Lessons
Center occupation can force an immediate response. Track rook-path blockers carefully: occupied central squares can deny edge pieces access even when the destination itself is empty.

### Position read
We hold the lower center squares: Red at (4,3), Yellow at (4,4). The opponent answered our opening by moving Blue to (3,3); (3,4) remains empty. No losses or eliminations. Green’s edge pieces cannot reach (3,4) horizontally because Blue at (3,3) blocks that row, and cannot reach the lower center through Red.

### Our plan
If still legal, use Red to take (3,4), securing three center squares and restricting Blue at (3,3). Then seek to occupy (3,3) after Blue leaves or capture the intruder through a same-color sandwich/enclosure. Preserve both lower-center pieces; watch for vertical attacks and friendly-fire capture lines.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent immediately recognized and contested the center, committing Blue from (3,7) to (3,3).

### Lessons
Coordinate center entries so one color does not block the other’s rook lane. Yellow at (4,4) leaves Red’s column-4 route to (3,4) open.

### Position read
We occupy (4,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow. The opponent occupies (3,3) with Blue and has advanced Green to (2,4), blocking Red’s direct descent from (0,4). Red has now developed to (3,5). No losses or eliminations.

### Our plan
The Red at (3,5) makes Blue’s move from (3,3) to (3,4) tactically vulnerable: Red at (4,3) can then land on (3,3), sandwiching Blue against (3,5). Continue building same-color flanks around the center, preserve our two lower-center occupants, and seek a route to (3,4) or a capture of the Blue intruder. Watch Green at (2,4) as both a blocker and a possible mixed capture target.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests key lanes promptly: Blue entered (3,3), then Green blocked column 4 at (2,4).

### Lessons
Center control must be backed by same-color geometry. Teammate pieces occupy center but cannot complete sandwiches for each other.

### Position read
We have Yellow at (4,4), Red at (3,5), and now Yellow at (4,1). Blue controls (3,3) and (5,3); the latter captured our Red at (4,3), giving Red 1 loss. Green remains at (2,4). No color is eliminated.

### Our plan
Yellow (4,1) blocks Green’s row-4 approach from the left. If an opponent enters (4,3) while Yellow remains at (4,4), slide Yellow (4,1) to (4,2) to sandwich it. Keep Red (3,5) as a barrier against Blue’s right-side access to (3,4). Build same-color capture geometry before attempting further center occupation, and seek to dislodge Blue from (3,3) or (5,3).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center and exploits exact same-color flanks: Blue used its pieces at (3,3) and (5,3) to capture Red at (4,3).

### Lessons
A piece moved into an existing sandwich is safe until a later qualifying move triggers capture. Protect central squares with latent landing moves, not merely stationary endpoints.

### Position read
Red moved (0,2) to (3,2), sandwiching Blue (3,3) and Green (3,4) against Red (3,5); both should be removed and each opponent color reaches 1 loss. We retain Red at (3,2),(3,5), Yellow at (4,1),(4,4). Blue remains at (5,3) plus right-edge pieces; Green is mainly on the left edge.

### Our plan
Use the Red pair across row 3 as a reusable capture frame while cautiously tightening the center. Yellow should preserve (4,4) and exploit (4,1) as a mobile landing piece if an opponent occupies (4,2) or (4,3). Seek one capture on each opposing color, then tactical elimination at 3 losses. Watch for attacks on Red (3,2) from left-edge Green and on Red (3,5) from the right.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent aggressively occupies central squares and recognizes same-color sandwich geometry. Green reinforced Blue’s center despite forming a mixed-color line vulnerable to Red’s same-color endpoints.

### Lessons
Mixed opposing colors are captured together in a sandwich. Before contesting a center square directly, scan for a landing square that brackets an entire mixed line against an existing same-color piece.

### Position read
After Red’s mixed sandwich, the opponent has 1 loss in each color; we have Red at (3,2),(3,5) framing row 3 and Yellow at (4,1),(4,4) framing row 4. Blue’s exposed piece is at (5,3), with another at (2,5). Yellow advanced (7,3) to (6,3), making a direct sandwich threat.

### Our plan
Next Yellow can play (4,1)->(4,3), capturing Blue (5,3) against Yellow (6,3), unless Blue evacuates. Use the forced tempo to strengthen the center with Red while preserving same-color endpoints. Seek a second loss against each opposing color, then tactical elimination at 3. Keep watch on Blue’s potential (4,7)->(4,5), which could capture Red (3,5) against Blue (2,5).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center aggressively and may accept central exposure, but recognizes sandwich geometry. Expect Blue (5,3) to retreat when its capture becomes immediate.

### Lessons
Threatening a sandwich can gain tempo even without an immediate capture. Preserve same-color frames and account for friendly fire whenever mixed allied pieces lie between endpoints.

### Position read
We moved Red (3,2)->(3,3). Our center foothold is Red (3,3) and Yellow (4,4); Red (0,4) can reach (3,4). Blue (5,3) is threatened by Yellow’s frame (4,1)/(6,3), while Red (3,5) remains vulnerable to Blue (4,7)->(4,5) against Blue (2,5). Losses: we have Red 1, Yellow 0; opponent has 1 in each color.

### Our plan
Prioritize the center win. If Blue (5,3) moves to (4,3), play Yellow (4,1)->(4,2), capturing it against Yellow (4,4). Otherwise, if (4,3) is open, play Yellow (4,1)->(4,3), usually also capturing Blue (5,3) against Yellow (6,3). Then place Red (0,4)->(3,4) and finish the remaining central square with Yellow.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests urgent geometry and may sacrifice tempo to block the center. Check every Blue reply for a central occupation or capture that disrupts our three-move sequence.

### Lessons
Center occupation can create a forcing race stronger than piece preservation. A blocker on (4,3) is tactically vulnerable because Yellow (4,4) supplies the same-color far flank.

### Position read
We now occupy three center squares: Red (3,3), Yellow (4,3), and Yellow (4,4). Red (3,5) is adjacent to the vacant final center square (3,4). Losses: we have Red 1, Yellow 0; the opponent has 1 in each color.

### Our plan
On Red’s next turn, play (3,5)->(3,4) to complete all four central squares and win immediately. Use this adjacent Red route even if Green blocks the separate vertical route from (0,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent withdrew Blue from (5,3), conceding the central tempo. Check Green’s move for any unexpected capture of a central piece, but its current geometry appears unable to remove or occupy the final square.

### Lessons
When two routes can fill the last center square, distinguish blocking one route from actually preventing center occupation.

### Position read
We completed the center with Red (3,5)->(3,4), joining Red (3,3) and Yellow (4,3),(4,4). This satisfies center occupation and wins immediately.

### Our plan
The game is won by center occupation.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent’s last Green move did not disrupt our three-piece center formation or block Red’s adjacent finishing move.

### Lessons
When the four central squares can be completed legally, center victory is immediate and takes priority over longer capture plans.
